patient_information: A 34-year-old Malawian woman, divorced, with no children, works as a street vendor selling mobile phone vouchers, and lives in an urban high-density area.
chief_complaint: Slowly progressive weakness of the left arm and leg.
history_of_present_illness: Problems started approximately 3 months earlier with a limp in her left leg, which progressed to affect her left arm over the following weeks. The onset was insidious and slowly progressive. She denies head trauma, headache, recent fever, nausea, visual impairment, or weight loss. She was diagnosed with smear-positive pulmonary tuberculosis 5 months earlier and was found to be HIV-reactive with a baseline CD4 count of 54/µL, for which she was started on antituberculous therapy, vitamin B6, antiretroviral therapy, and co-trimoxazole prophylaxis.
exposure_and_epidemiology: Lives in an urban high-density area and works as a street vendor selling mobile phone vouchers.
vitals: Afebrile, vital signs normal, apart from slightly pale conjunctivae.
physical_exam: Spastic hemiparesis on the left with hyperreflexia. Left leg power is 2/5 (active movement with gravity eliminated) and left arm power is 3/5 (active movement against gravity). Pronator drift on the left indicates proximal weakness. Sensation of pain is reduced in her left leg and hand. Cranial nerves examination is normal. Fundi are normal without signs of papilloedema or retinitis.
labs_and_diagnostics: Full blood count: WBC 3.8 × 10º/L, haemoglobin 9.9g/dL, platelets 140×109/L. Baseline CD4 count of 54/µL. Routine CSF examination was normal, India Ink stain and fungal cultures were negative. Head MRI showed multifocal T2 hyperintense lesions exclusively affecting the white matter, more prominent in the right hemisphere (frontal and temporal lobes), and a small area of demyelination in the left cerebellar peduncle.
differential_diagnosis: Cerebral toxoplasmosis, progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML), CNS lymphoma, cryptococcoma, CMV encephalitis, Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection (tuberculoma or tuberculous abscess), brain tumour, brain metastases, cerebral abscess, neurocysticercosis, neuroschistosomiasis, Chagas' disease, and immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome (IRIS) related conditions.
management_and_clinical_course: Patient was already on antituberculous therapy, vitamin B6, antiretroviral therapy, and co-trimoxazole prophylaxis. Initially started on empirical antitoxoplasmosis treatment with high-dose co-trimoxazole, continued ART and antituberculous treatment, and added Prednisolone 1 mg/kg for presumed IRIS. After 4 weeks, clinical status was unchanged. At 8 weeks, further deterioration of left hand power occurred, leading to an MRI which revealed findings suggestive of PML. The patient was referred to a local rehabilitation centre for walking aids and palliative care team.
final_diagnosis: Presumed diagnosis of Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML).

images.caption: Pronator drift on the left side as a sign of left upper limb weakness. The patient was asked to stretch out both arms and close her eyes.
Cranial CT scan showing a hypodense lesion in the subcortical white matter in the left occipital lobe.
Cranial MRI showing bilateral T2 hyperintense (to grey matter) lesions in the subcortical white matter involving the so-called U-fibres resulting in a "scalloped appearance".
